s.t: Tomás Méndez wrote the song Caetano Veloso sings here in 1954, and Pedro Infante sang it on screen in the 1955 Mexican comedy Escuela de vagabundos.
s.q: It initially appeared in the classic Mexican comedy Escuela de vagabundos screened in 1955, where it was sung by the star of the film, Pedro Infante.

s.t: Caetano Veloso recalled that Brazilians saw ‘Cucurrucucú Paloma’ as vulgar, kitsch and sentimental, and that at a party someone bet he lacked the courage to record it.
s.src: The story of a song: Cucurrucucú Paloma (Veloso + Almodóvar)
s.q: one of the most vulgar, kitsch, sentimental examples of Spanish-American song … I bet you don't have the courage to record Cucurrucucú

s.t: In Pedro Almodóvar's Talk to Her, Caetano Veloso sings it in an art-song style quite different from the mariachi folk-kitsch of the song's original 1955 film presentation.
s.q: the piece is rendered by the Brazilian singer Caetano Veloso in an art-song style quite different from the mariachi folk-kitsch of its original cinema presentation.

s.t: The Italian singer Franco Battiato borrowed this song's refrain for his own ‘Cuccurucucù’, on his album La voce del padrone.
s.q: the refrain was also taken up by Franco Battiato in his own song "Cuccurucucù" (on La voce del padrone).

f.t: Interrogators asked whether he had sung Brazil's anthem to the tune of ‘Tropicália’; he said that was impossible, as the anthem's verses have ten syllables and the song's eight.
f.q: asked Caetano whether he had sung the national anthem of Brazil to the melody of "Tropicália," to which Caetano responded that it would be impossible because the verses of the Brazilian anthem are decasyllable and the verses of "Tropicalia" only have eight poetic syllables.

f.t: Booed at a 1968 festival, he told students “if you are the same in politics as you are in aesthetics, we're done for!” then finished the song out of tune.
f.q: "...if you are the same in politics as you are in aesthetics, we're done for!" ... He then deliberately finished the song out of tune

f.t: His 1967 festival performance of ‘Alegria, Alegria’ with the group Beat Boys, alongside Gilberto Gil backed by Os Mutantes, was the first time rock bands had played the festival.
f.q: this marked the first time that rock bands had performed at the festival.

f.t: In 1994, he made Fina Estampa, an album sung entirely in Spanish to reaffirm his bond with Latin American music; it won the Prêmio Sharp for Best Foreign Album.
f.q: undertook a major project to reaffirm his relationship with Latin American music ... an album sung entirely in Spanish ... Prêmio Sharp award as Best Foreign Album
